previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of COPD, chronic alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted with worsening cough, green sputum, subjective fever, and hypoxemia. He was initially uncooperative in the ED but became alert and oriented on admission, though tremulous. He reported heavy alcohol use, last drink 12 hours prior, and symptoms consistent with alcohol withdrawal. Labs showed hypernatremia, which improved with IV fluids. A chest X-ray revealed new lung opacities suggestive of pneumonia. He was treated with levofloxacin, metronidazole, prednisone, and nebulizers for COPD exacerbation and pneumonia, and diazepam for alcohol withdrawal. Hypertension was managed with amlodipine. Despite clinical improvement, he eloped from the hospital on the third day before completing treatment or receiving discharge instructions.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo man with COPD and chronic alcoholism admitted for COPD 
exacerbation, RML collapse and intoxication.  
 
# COPD exacerbation: he has chronic lung disease with active 
smoking ___ pack per day). He was recently treated for a 
pneumonia in ___, however presented also with new RML 
collapse. Exam showed diffuse rhonchi and scattered wheezes. He 
was treated with prednisone 40 mg and azithromycin x 4 days (did 
not complete 5-day course as he left prior to receiving 
prescriptions), standing ipratropium / albuterol, guiafenisin, 
and supplemental O2. At the time that he eloped, he had a 
persistent non-productive cough, however his lung sounds were 
clear, and he maintained O2 saturation in mid-90s on room air. 
 
# EtOH abuse: He has chronic alcoholism, and has had multiple 
admissions for this issue. This is clearly a significant barrier 
to his self care and mangement of chronic medical issues. He was 
seen by psychiatry and social work many times without signifanct 
progress towards rehabilitation. He was treated with valium prn 
CIWA, IV thiamine, folate and MVI. He received a total of 120mg 
diazepam during this admission, and at the time of discharge, 
was he was mildly agitated however did not have other evidence 
of withdrawal. He was encouraged to attend AA, however left 
prior to receiving his paperwork and scripts (eloped).
  
# Right olecranon fractureulna: sustained in ___ after a 
fall while intoxicated. Was reduced in the ED at that visit with 
a planned surgical fixation as an outpatient, however he did not 
follow up in clinic. His arm was in a sling on presentation, and 
had an intact sensory, motor and vascular exam. He was treated 
with tylenol, tramadol, and oxycodone 10mg TID for pain while in 
house, but was not discharged on this medication. Ortho 
recommended working with physical therapy, and following up as 
an outpatient (Dr. ___ in 2 wks) for possible elective 
repair in several weeks.
 
# Hypertension: He was hypertensive with SBP 160-170s on 
admission, likely essential hypertension exacerbated by pain and 
EtOH withdrawal. He was treated with amlodipine 10mg during this 
admission, however left before he was provided a script for his 
medications (eloped).
 
# Suicidality: He was seen by psych in the ED, and he did not 
have suicidality and did not require 1:1 sitter during this 
admission.
